question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & 3 & 3 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & 6 & 7 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form. Select the resulting augmented matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & 3 & 3 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & 6 & 7 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=-\frac{1}{3}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ -3 & 3 & 6 & 7 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(3)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{4}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{4}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

metadata.domain: x,y,z real; p,q,s nonzero; nonsingular 3-by-3 coefficient matrix

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -2 & -4 & 4 \\ -3 & 3 & 4 & -8 \\ 1 & -4 & -4 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -2 & -4 & 4 \\ -3 & 3 & 4 & -8 \\ 1 & -4 & -4 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ -3 & 3 & 4 & -8 \\ 1 & -4 & -4 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(3)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 1 & -4 & -4 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=1 \\ y &=-\frac{4}{3}-\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)(1) \\ &=-2 \\ x &=2-(-1)(-2) \\ &\quad -(-2)(1) \\ &=2\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(2,-2,1\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x-6y-2z &=-2 \\ 3x+9y+z &=8 \\ -2x-9y-3z &=-4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -6 & -2 & -2 \\ 3 & 9 & 1 & 8 \\ -2 & -9 & -3 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 9 & 1 & 8 \\ -2 & -9 & -3 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-3)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 5 \\ -2 & -9 & -3 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -3 & -1 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-\frac{5}{2} \\ y &=\frac{2}{3}-\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{5}{2}\right) \\ &=\frac{3}{2} \\ x &=1-(3)\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) \\ &\quad -(1)\left(-\frac{5}{2}\right) \\ &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-1,\frac{3}{2},-\frac{5}{2}\right)
$$

$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & 9 & -3 & -15 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 & -11 \\ 2 & 8 & -5 & -12\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & -1 & -5 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 & -11 \\ 2 & 8 & -5 & -12\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 8 & -5 & -12\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=\frac{1}{2}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{2} & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{2} & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{2} & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-\frac{1}{2} \\ y &=-1-\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) \\ &=-\frac{7}{4} \\ x &=-5-(3)\left(-\frac{7}{4}\right) \\ &\quad -(-1)\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) \\ &=-\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-\frac{1}{4},-\frac{7}{4},-\frac{1}{2}\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y+2z &=-10 \\ 3x-6y &=-16 \\ x-5y+4z &=-3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -4 & 2 & -10 \\ 3 & -6 & 0 & -16 \\ 1 & -5 & 4 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -5 \\ 3 & -6 & 0 & -16 \\ 1 & -5 & 4 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-3)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & -5 & 4 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -\frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -\frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -\frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=\frac{1}{3} \\ y &=-\frac{2}{3}-(-1)\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \\ &=-\frac{1}{3} \\ x &=-5-(-2)\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) \\ &\quad -(1)\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \\ &=-6\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-6,-\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{3}\right)
$$
